texture_overrides_note: WIRED's homepage is a broadsheet plugged into a wall socket: committed paper-white canvas (#ffffff) with no cards and no shadows, near-black Page Ink (#1a1a1a, 17.4:1) for headlines and body, Caption Gray (#757575, 4.6:1) for the muted ladder, and exactly one accent that matters, the saturated Link Blue (#057dbc, 4.5:1 on white, clearing the 3.0 editorial floor). Per WIRED's rule the blue stays scarce, one interactive cue per beat, never a fill or second color, and the page stays in pure grayscale otherwise. Fraunces at 600 substitutes for the proprietary WiredDisplay serif (a high-contrast didone face with the same newsstand presence) and carries the headline and italic pull-quote; Inter substitutes for Apercu on body and UI; the terminal and any mono block render in JetBrains Mono, which stands in for the WiredMono uppercase kickers and timestamps. Corners are square (stage_radius 0, border-radius 0 is law) and rules are the printerly 2px. Texture is deliberately restrained because WIRED is flat by religion: grain 0.03 for a faint newsprint tooth, vignette 0.10 for a soft edge on the white stock, halation 0.03 so emphasis beats still bloom faintly, lighting_arc 0.22 for the time-of-day drift the WOW gate wants without breaking the paper-white contract.
